newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: IATA pledges help to solve Madrid airport problems.
newsitem.headline: IATA pledges help to solve Madrid airport problems.

text.p: The International Air Transport Association pledged support on Thursday for efforts to solve capacity problems at Madrid's Barajas airport, saying scheduling should improve once construction work is finished.

IATA, grouping 254 of the world's leading airlines, said a huge increase in demand at peak periods combined with a major construction project as well as bad weather had caused scheduling problems at Barajas.

In a joint statement with the International Air Carriers' Association (IACA), IATA said that instigating a peak scheduling profile and an airport capacity assessment could help solve some of the problems in the short term.
It added that the Spanish Airport and Airspace Authority was working hard to improve operations at the airport.
